items.title: Iran-Israel War, Yet No $200 Oil | Why Crude Hasn't Exploded Despite West Asia Tensions
items.description: Despite months of conflict between Iran and Israel and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices have remained below the feared $100-$200 range. China's reduced crude imports, OPEC+ supply increases and repeated ceasefire signals have helped cap prices. Here's why the global oil market hasn't panicked yet—and why India is watching closely.
